english.title: Care provider breach duty of care resulting in ill-treatment / neglect of individual
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), were a care provider when an individual, namely **(..SPECIFY NAME OF CARE WORKER..), who had care of another, namely **(..SPECIFY NAME OF VICTIM..), by virtue of being part of your arrangements, ill-treated or wilfully neglected that individual, your activities having been managed or organised in a way which amounted to a gross breach of a relevant duty of care owed by you to the individual who was ill-treated or neglected and, in the absence of the breach, the ill-treatment or wilful neglect would not have occurred or would have been less likely to have occurred
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 21(1) and 23(1) of the Criminal Justice and Courts Act 2015.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
care provider
had an individual having care of another by virtue of being part of arrangements
who ill-treated / wilfully neglected that individual
the activities of the care provider having been managed/organised in way which amounted to gross breach of duty of care owed to the individual
in the absence of breach, the ill-treatment / neglect would not have occurred / would have been less likely

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Definitions of terms used in this offence can be found in section 21(2) - (9).
(ii) A court before which a person is convicted of this offence may make either or both of the following orders -
(a) a remedial order;
(b) a publicity order;
whether instead of or as well as imposing a fine - see section 23 of the Act for further details.
